key_insight: AI-guided screening identifies Li-intercalated ZrS₂ as a promising thermal switch, with lithiation sharply reducing cross-plane heat transport through framework softening and enhanced phonon scattering.
engineering_relevance: Electrochemically controlled thermal switching could enable adaptive thermal management and pulsed waste-heat recovery.
method: Screen 57 TMDC candidates using universal machine-learned interatomic potentials and DFT.
Evaluate 1T and 2H phases with Li and Mg intercalation.
Analyze phonon transport and model device-level waste-heat recovery.
evidence_signal: Calculations predict that Li₀.₁₂₅ZrS₂ lowers cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (~74-fold contrast); device modelling reaches 86% of an ideal switch’s recovered energy.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed to establish switching speed, cycling stability, and practical intercalation control.
paper_title: High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials
